full_statement: Let $\mathcal S=\{S_1,\ldots,S_m\}$ be a set system on ground set $[n]$, and suppose every element belongs to at most $t$ sets. Equivalently, let $A\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}$ be an incidence matrix whose columns have at most $t$ ones. A signing $x\in\{-1,+1\}^n$ colors the elements red and blue, and its discrepancy is $\|Ax\|_\infty=\max_{r\le m}|\sum_{j\in S_r}x_j|$. Beck and Fiala proved discrepancy at most $2t-1$. The Beck-Fiala conjecture asks whether there is a universal constant $C$ such that every degree-$t$ set system has a signing with discrepancy at most $C\sqrt t$, independent of $m$ and $n$. The historically open problem is to prove this dimension-free $O(\sqrt t)$ bound for every relation among $t,m,n$, or to construct a family of degree-$t$ set systems with discrepancy $\omega(\sqrt t)$. Results that work only when $t$ is large compared with $n$, or that retain a residual $\sqrt{\log n}$ term, are partial progress but do not settle the conjecture. Status at 2026-11-09: Guo, Fang, and Lu's September 2026 preprint claims the full Beck-Fiala conjecture via its Komlos theorem and Corollary 1.2. This record flags a claimed resolution, pending verification.
background: Historical context before the 2026 full-resolution claims: Combinatorial discrepancy asks whether a set system can be two-colored so that every set sees nearly the same number of red and blue elements. Beck-Fiala studies the sparse case where each element appears in at most $t$ sets. The original theorem gives discrepancy at most $2t-1$, while the conjecture predicts the much smaller bound $O(\sqrt t)$ independent of the number of sets and elements. This is a central problem because it sits between sparse set systems, vector balancing, rounding, and discrepancy algorithms. It is also implied by the more general Komlos conjecture. Recent work by Bansal and Jiang goes beyond the Banaszczyk bound and resolves the conjecture for high-degree regimes such as $t\ge \log^2 n$, but the full range of $t$ was not settled by those earlier results. Status at 2026-11-09: Guo, Fang, and Lu's September 2026 preprint claims the full Beck-Fiala conjecture via its Komlos theorem and Corollary 1.2.
open_problem: Verify the claimed resolution of the original conjecture. Historical target: Prove or refute the Beck-Fiala conjecture: every degree-$t$ set system has discrepancy $O(\sqrt t)$.
known_results:
Historical context before the 2026 full-resolution claims: Beck and Fiala proved the original $2t-1$ bound. Bukh slightly improved the linear bound to $2t-O(\log^*t)$, but this remains far from square-root behavior. Banaszczyk's vector-balancing theorem implies $O(\sqrt{t\log n})$, which has the conjectured dependence on $t$ but retains a dimension factor. Bansal-Dadush-Garg made Banaszczyk-type bounds algorithmic. Bansal and Jiang recently improved the landscape: they resolve Beck-Fiala for $t\ge\log^2 n$ and give bounds of the form $\widetilde O(\sqrt t+\sqrt{\log n})$ in the remaining regime, improving on $O(\sqrt{t\log n})$. These results also provide efficient algorithms for the colorings they guarantee. The dimension-free $O(\sqrt t)$ statement for every $t$, especially small and intermediate $t$ relative to $n$, was not settled by those earlier results. Status at 2026-11-09: Guo, Fang, and Lu's September 2026 preprint claims the full Beck-Fiala conjecture via its Komlos theorem and Corollary 1.2.

Algorithmic follow-up: Guo, Fang, and Lu, arXiv:2609.23540v2, Corollary 1.2, report a deterministic real-RAM algorithm with discrepancy below $16544\sqrt t$. Xiaoyu Li, arXiv:2609.30044v1, Corollary 1.2, improves this to below $99\sqrt t$, with a polynomial-bit implementation on rational inputs. These are algorithmic square-root guarantees for all degree regimes, not only existential or high-degree results. The full proofs have not been independently certified here.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Check the cited full-resolution and algorithmic theorems, including precision and computational-model assumptions. Treat any new target about sharp constants as a separate question.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A proof must give a bound $C\sqrt t$ with a universal constant $C$ independent of $m,n$, row sizes, and any distributional assumption on the set system. The signing must color all elements, not merely give a partial coloring unless the iteration is fully specified without accumulating extra logarithmic loss. A verifier should check quantifiers carefully: results assuming $t\ge\log^2 n$, bounds such as $\widetilde O(\sqrt t+\sqrt{\log n})$, smoothed/random incidence matrices, hereditary discrepancy under extra assumptions, or algorithms whose failure probability is only over a restricted input distribution are partial progress. A counterexample must prove a worst-case lower bound $\omega(\sqrt t)$ for degree-$t$ set systems, not merely show that a particular algorithm fails. The relevant theorem statements and proof framework were read, but this audit is not an independent proof verification; no peer-reviewed publication was established.
